new.n: Counterfeiters' cave on Pine Run, Brandon Twp (Cooley gang, 1856-57)
new.pl: Isaiah Cooley 160, N½ sec 27 T85N R1E, Brandon Twp, S of Emeline (1893 plat); the cave on 'Pine Run' is not fixed
new.st: The 1910 county history tells of a counterfeiters' cave on Pine Run in Brandon Twp used by Isaiah Cooley's gang in 1856-57; Washburn, the die-maker, died in 1858. The 1893 plat puts Cooley's 160 acres in the N½ of sec 27, south of Emeline, with an unnamed creek running past it. Pin is the Cooley tract, not the cave.
new.t: Relic site (dies, bogus coin); county history only. The creek named Pine Run is not on the plat. Private farmland: permission.
src: Ellis, History of Jackson County, Iowa (1910), vol. 1, pp. 342-343

set.st: The county history tells of an eccentric Scotchman named Smith who lived at the Whitford cabin on the Fergus Falls townsite and was killed by Indians in 1862; a tale grew that he buried gold on the townsite, and a gold sovereign was later found near the old cabin. By 1916 the cabin cellar lay 'near Whitford street, inside the fence of Henry G. Page's block'. Pin is the N half of the Page block, not the spot itself.
set.pl: Henry G. Page block, E side of N. Whitford St (block 64, N half near E. Summit), Fergus Falls; the Whitford cabin cellar lay inside his fence (1916)
pinev: 1900 census: Henry G. Page, b. 1832 NH, wife Alice, 219 Whitford St.

Sanborn, Fergus Falls, Jan 1903, sheet 7: N. Whitford St between E. Summit and E. Cavour; the E (river) side is block 64, numbered new-even / old-odd (200/201, 204/205, 208, 212 church, 222/223), so old 219 = the N half of block 64 near E. Summit.
Placed from MnGeo address points: E side of N. Whitford St between E. Cavour (46.2845) and E. Summit (46.2855); modern 222 N Whitford is at 46.2852,-96.0704. r100.
